<reason>B defeated the proposition’s universal prerequisite with a narrowly targeted encampment prohibition that preserves stable, lawful outdoor alternatives without providing the full shelter, storage, and services package. A conceded that such a standing rule could be justified, then tried to exclude it by definition or characterize it as satisfying conditions it lacked. A’s compelling objections to blanket criminalization did not answer B’s constrained alternative. B also explained the substantive benefit: protecting clinic access without forcing residents into perpetual displacement.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s second rebuttal decisively identified both A’s concession of a justified standing rule and A’s insertion of “storage and outreach” into a hypothetical supplying neither. This directly defeated A’s claim that B had conceded the motion’s availability requirement.</best_rebuttal>
